name: InfiniteGraph
tagline: Objectivity's distributed graph database for Java and C++; discontinued after the vendor ceased in 2023.
description: InfiniteGraph was a distributed graph database from Objectivity, Inc., first released around 2010 and built on the storage and federation technology of Objectivity/DB. It modelled data as a labelled, directed multigraph in which edges are first-class objects, supported fully ACID transactions with subgraph update locking alongside relaxed, non-blocking concurrent ingest, and was queried through its 'DO' query language, a traversal and navigation API, and path pattern matching. A federation could address up to 65,535 databases, and it was used in government, telecom and cybersecurity analytics. A rebuilt InfiniteGraph appeared in 2021 with another release announced in 2023, but Objectivity reportedly ceased operations in late 2023 and no product or support remains.
statusNote: Objectivity, Inc. reportedly ceased operations in late 2023; objectivity.com no longer serves product pages and no support is available.

scale.notes: Federated databases with 64-bit object IDs; up to 65,535 databases per federation.

strengths: Edges are first-class objects with their own identity
ACID transactions with optional relaxed concurrent ingest
Federation scaled to very large distributed graphs
Combined graph navigation with object-style queries
weaknesses: Vendor gone; no downloads, updates or support
Proprietary 'DO' query language with no ecosystem
useCases: Historical reference for federated graph databases
